clue.text: Was the deciding factor that upset the balance

definitions.meaning: proved decisive, settled the matter one way
literally made a pair of weighing pans swing down on one side

explanation.surface: Something proved decisive by disturbing an equilibrium.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being decisive comes from a weight added to one pan making a balance drop, which is literally disturbing it.

clue.text: Where to stay dry?

parts.note: dry here means teetotal, not out of the rain: a lodging place serving no alcohol

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where they might keep out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' suggests shelter from rain, but it means abstaining from alcohol; such hotels were common in Victorian Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel run on abstinence principles serves no drink, so guests remain sober there.

clue.text: Finished up in the brine rather drunk

definitions.meaning: preserved in salt water or vinegar, like onions

explanation.surface: Someone who fell into the sea ended up somewhat tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Food steeped in brine is preserved this way, and the same word is slang for being sozzled.

clue.text: River Avon

definitions.meaning: Anthony ..., the Prime Minister, was made Earl of Avon

explanation.surface: A bare name: the Avon is a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface equates two rivers, but 'Avon' points to the title the Prime Minister Anthony Eden took on retiring, Earl of Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cumbrian river shares its name with the statesman whose peerage title was Avon.

clue.text: Joined together the rein in that place

explanation.surface: A horseman knots the reins together where they stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined together' simply tells you to run the two words into one.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning within that thing or location, as in legal documents.

clue.text: Love twitch in ear possibly caused by amatory literature

indicators.note: signals that the pieces may be rearranged into another order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch in someone's ear is blamed on reading racy books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles O, TIC and EAR together; 'in' and 'caused by' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic writing is literature concerned with sexual love.

clue.text: Quote it in church

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Read this passage aloud during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention a passage or source as evidence is to quote it.

clue.text: Appearing to be watching

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be observing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form means both seeming (she is pale-faced) and using one's eyes to observe.

clue.text: Post free

parts.note: a post is a job, a situation

explanation.surface: A postal item is sent without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests postage paid; read instead as a job that is unfilled, the heading of old job advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: A job opening waiting to be filled is a position with nobody in it.

clue.text: Came the revolution, used this weapon?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: When the uprising arrived, rebels took up this blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' is the anagram signal working on CAME THE; the whole clue also pictures rebels with blades.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used as a tool and as an arm, typical of Latin American revolts.

clue.text: Letters sent to a remote settlement

definitions.meaning: outgoing mail, read as two words: out and post

explanation.surface: Mail is dispatched to a far-off colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word is outgoing mail; whole it is a far-flung station or settlement.

clue.text: Girl, note, takes everything back

indicators.note: the word for everything is written right to left after the note

explanation.surface: A girl writes a note and retracts all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the note to the reversed word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in the jazz singer Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Agencies that inform me before help returns

indicators.note: the word for help comes back, so it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone asks newspapers to tell them things before assistance arrives back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns only the word for help; 'before' is a joining word that keeps ME at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Press, radio and television are the channels through which the public is informed.

clue.text: Mark on passport is in Virginia

indicators.note: the small word is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A traveller's passport is stamped in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry permit is a stamp or endorsement put on a travel document.

clue.text: Cry softly with model at the burial-place

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: A mourner weeps quietly beside a fashion model at the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground vault beneath a church, used for burials.

clue.text: This is a short account of Biblical character

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A brief description summing up a figure from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of Abraham and Sarah in Genesis.

clue.text: And even a firedog

parts.note: to even something is to iron it flat

explanation.surface: Just a fireside fixture, and a level one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal stand on a hearth holding logs is another name for a firedog.

clue.text: Stupid person for instance has first-class spear

parts.note: EG, short for exempli gratia, means for instance
A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A fool owns an excellent spear, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender iron-tipped throwing spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Where to find the driver's seat in area frequently used as a battleground

definitions.text: Where to find the driver's seat
definitions.meaning: the pilot's or racing driver's compartment

definitions.text: area frequently used as a battleground
definitions.meaning: a pit for cockfighting, hence any arena of repeated conflict

explanation.surface: A driver's seat sits in a place often fought over.
explanation.walkthrough: Belgium was called 'the cockpit of Europe' for its many battles.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the control compartment of a racing car or plane and an arena for cockfights, hence a site of frequent wars.

clue.text: Whip round nude floor show

indicators.note: the whip surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a cat is a whip, as in cat-o'-nine-tails

explanation.surface: Hats are passed round for a naked performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip round' looks like a collection of money for someone, but 'round' is the container signal and the whip is a cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment performed at a nightclub or restaurant while patrons dine or drink.

clue.text: After being silent we object to the Roman orator

indicators.note: the pronoun follows the word for silent

parts.note: US is the object form of we

explanation.surface: Having held their tongues, the crowd protest against the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a protest, but it is grammar: the object case of 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman historian was also celebrated as an orator in the courts.

clue.text: After tea smile but show annoyance

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone smiles after their cuppa but still looks vexed.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress or vexation at a failure or humiliation.

clue.text: Be unseated — successfully?

definitions.meaning: fall off, as from a horse
to succeed, as in the plan worked out well

explanation.surface: A rider is thrown, and asks whether that went well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both falling from a mount and turning out well.

clue.text: Recovered on court?

parts.note: regained strength, with a nod to the long exchanges of shots in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player bounced back during the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain health or form; also, on a tennis court, to exchange a long series of strokes.

clue.text: Spanish oboist holding vagrant

indicators.note: the two words contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A Spanish musician on the oboe shelters a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A wandering homeless person or itinerant worker, in American usage.

clue.text: Rascal has most of the prawns

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A rogue grabs the bulk of the seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child or rogue.

clue.text: Insect jumps from leaf

indicators.note: letters that jump about land in a new order

explanation.surface: A small bug leaps off a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingless jumping parasite of mammals and birds.

clue.text: Skeletal part remaining when tree is removed from the bonfire

indicators.note: the tree's letters are taken out of the other word

explanation.surface: After a tree is pulled out of the fire, a bit of skeleton is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Any piece of the hard tissue forming a skeleton.

clue.text: Pretty loud music

parts.note: F is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: Rather noisy tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adverb with 'loud', but it is the definition, meaning lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive or beautiful, as in a lady of good looks.

clue.text: Drive out of gear

explanation.surface: Someone takes a car out of gear.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to expel; as a noun it means outfit or equipment.

clue.text: Wind instrument from Cairo an unusual design

indicators.note: these letters are set out in an unusual new pattern

explanation.surface: A flute brought from Egypt has an odd shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Landlords who have a good reputation for paying bills

definitions.text: Landlords who have a good reputation
definitions.meaning: people who let property, of good standing
documents from a bank guaranteeing payment

explanation.surface: Trustworthy landlords pay their accounts promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bank documents guaranteeing a buyer's payment; whimsically, lessors of good standing.
